subject: RAG qualification — proposed evals, retrieval knobs, and next steps for Acetech
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jacobs <emma@acetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RAG qualification — proposed evals, retrieval knobs, and next steps for Acetech

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Emma — great to learn more about the Acetech search+assistant use case and the real-world constraints you have on latency and auditability. Summary and proposed next steps below.

Quick summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: reduce agent-level hallucinations in product-help flows while keeping end-to-end latency <= 700ms for the first token in your web UI.
- Content: ~120k docs (support KB, release notes, short how-tos), chunking currently at ~1,600 chars.
- Current infra: embeddings in-house (open-source) and a vector DB; no reranker in production today.

Redwood recommendations (short-term eval plan)
1) Candidate models to benchmark (hosted + quantized dedicated):
   - small/generic: Mistral-7B-instruct (latency-friendly baseline)
   - mid: Llama-2-13B-q4 (best cost/quality tradeoff in our tests)
   - higher-quality: Orca-22B / RedAct-xxl (for quality ceiling checks)

2) Retrieval & reranker baseline config to test (controlled sweep)
   - Embedding model: text-embedding-3-small (we'll also test your in-house embeddings side-by-side)
   - Retriever: nprobe/top_k = 8, chunk_size = 512 tokens (approx 3–4 sentences)
   - Reranker: cross-encoder candidate (cross-encoder re-rank of top 16 -> final top 3) vs. bi-encoder-only (top 5)

3) Eval/benchmarks we'll run for POC (we'll share scripts and results):
   - Precision@1 and P@3 on your seeded queries (you to provide ~120 canonical queries)
   - Grounding score (percentage of model responses directly supported by one or more retrieved doc spans)
   - Hallucination rate (manual label on sampled 200 responses)
   - Latency profile (p50/p95 total RTT and token-first latency for each model/config)

Attachments included: prompt set (acetech_prompt_suite_v1.json), initial benchmark harness CSV (acetech_rag_benchmarks_v1.csv), suggested retrieval config (acetech_retrieval_config.yaml).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Emma: share 120 canonical queries + a sampled set of 200 end-user conversations (anonymized) — needed by 2028-03-09 to hit our proposed timeline.
- Redwood (Marissa): spin up benchmark harness + baseline runs with Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B (target: p50 latency < 400ms).
- Redwood (Karthik): prepare reranker experiments (cross-encoder config + featurization for your in-house embeddings).

Risks we flagged
- If your in-house embeddings are lower-dimension / lower-recall than our embedding candidates, we may need to increase top_k or adopt document expansion to keep P@1 high — this trades off latency and cost.
- Regression monitoring: we recommend adding automatic quality regression checks on the seeded queries (we'll provide a lightweight webhook-based alert if P@1 drops by >7% between model rollouts).

Proposed timeline
- Week 1 (by 2028-03-11): you send queries + sample conversations; Redwood provides initial harness and config.
- Week 2 (by 2028-03-18): baseline runs complete, reranker ablation started.
- Week 3 (by 2028-03-25): POC readout with recommended final config.

If this looks good I'll schedule a short 30-min sync next Wednesday to align engineers on inputs.

Cheers,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: acetech_prompt_suite_v1.json, acetech_rag_benchmarks_v1.csv, acetech_retrieval_config.yaml
From: Emma Jacobs <emma@acetech.com>

Subject: Re: RAG qualification — proposed evals, retrieval knobs, and next steps for Acetech

Thanks, Sean — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick clarifying Qs:
1) For the cross-encoder reranker, what's the expected latency delta? Our SLA for assistant-first-token is tight.
2) On the seeded queries: can we trim to 80 canonical queries if necessary?
3) Any compliance flags we should be aware of for running the mid/large models in a hosted vs dedicated environment?

We'll try to get you the query set by Friday (2028-03-09); if not, we'll prioritize 80 and flag which ones are higher value.

—Emma
Emma Jacobs
Head of Product — Acetech
emma@acetech.com
